items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: That's Lawrence Brown. I mean there's so many.

ctx.x: I was going to ask again, before I forget it, about Joe Oliver again. Was he really a good pool player? Did he play all the time? Who was that? Joe Oliver. Oh yeah, he was good. You know he had one bad eye.

And he's good, a good pool player. Yeah. He had one bad idea. Now you take Armani for the type of music that he played, he was all right. But I wouldn't put him in the same category as Earl Hines. And there's Teddy Wilson. Now there's Kate Johnson, another trombone player where he's playing, Bud Johnson's brother. He was wonderful I think too. After immediately he was Armstrong, he joined Armstrong. And he played some wonderful solos, breaks and things. So I mean there's so many. And there's Vic. Vic got a style…

I was going to ask you again to change the subject. We'll finish up in a few minutes now. About some of the New Orleans places like Miss Cole's Lawn Parties. Did you ever go there or were you just a kid?

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I got that, I started that because different trombone players, I liked the tone like Lawrence Brown, I even liked Seagarden, Higginbotham.

ctx.x: They still had Cadiz and Liberty.

Yeah, same place. And right around on Jenna I think it was, the two hall boys, they're the cousins to the Humphreys, you know. And I used to see them carrying the instruments. But still, I never thought about playing in the music, you see. And so you take, for instance, the vibrato you spoke about. I used to get more or less a straight tone, you understand. And when I first noticed that my tone was changing, I get more of a vibrato now than ever. I got that, I started that because different trombone players, I…
Well do you use lip or diaphragm or something?
